### Solution Steps:

1. **Given Data:**
   - Prism: Square base $40\text{ mm}$, height $60\text{ mm}$.
   - Position: Base on ground, one rectangular face parallel to and $10\text{ mm}$ behind the Picture Plane (PP).
   - Station Point (SP): $30\text{ mm}$ in front of PP, $80\text{ mm}$ above the Ground Plane (GP).
   - Central Plane (CP): $45\text{ mm}$ to the right of the center of the prism.

2. **Setup Reference Planes:**
   - Draw the Ground Line (GL) and Picture Plane (PP) line parallel to it at a convenient distance.
   - Draw the Top View (TV) of the square prism such that one face is $10\text{ mm}$ behind the PP line. The center of the prism is placed $45\text{ mm}$ to the left of the Central Plane line since the CP is $45\text{ mm}$ to the right of the prism center.

3. **Station Point & Visual Rays:**
   - Mark the Station Point in the Top View $30\text{ mm}$ in front of PP.
   - Draw top view lines from SP to all visible corners of the prism's top and bottom bases.

4. **Perspective View Construction:**
   - Draw the Horizon Line (HL) at a height of $80\text{ mm}$ above the Ground Line. Locate the Vanishing Point (VP) or use visual ray intersection method (interception of top view rays on the PP projected down to the Perspective Plane).
   - Project intersection points from the PP down to the respective height levels measured from the Ground Line to obtain the final perspective projection.
proTip: Carefully track the location of the Central Plane relative to the geometric center of the object to avoid mirroring errors.
